biography.plain_text: Daniel McLean McDonald was a British industrialist who founded Birmingham Sound Reproducers in 1932. An engineer who later qualified in medicine without practising, he developed a business known for automatic record changers. He sold his BSR shareholding in 1970 and subsequently became the principal shareholder of the precision-engineering firm Glenburn.

long_biography.plain_text:
British industrialist Daniel McLean McDonald studied how ancient societies weighed and measured the world around them. His research ranged across Egypt, Sumer and later cultures, examining connections between units of weight, volume and length. He was particularly interested in how measuring liquids linked these different systems. His papers became The Origins of Metrology, the first monograph published by the institute bearing his name.

His support also gave archaeological research a permanent base at Cambridge. A major gift enabled the creation of the McDonald Institute for Archaeological Research, which brought together scholars working across scientific and historical disciplines. Its activities included laboratories, publications and research funding.

uncertainties.detail: The rare full name and exact lifespan strongly resolve the person. A dealer listing for a 1959 Tamarind article naming Dr D. M. McDonald is only a weak lead and was unavailable on direct opening; it is not treated as primary ownership verification. No independent Galapagos Explorer bridge is claimed.

The 1970 BSR exit prevents treating later corporate assets as his. Glenburn is established only for an earlier post-exit period. A potentially relevant Portuguese capital-register lead was unreadable and is excluded. No unsupported 1991 business ownership or principal allocation is inferred.

McLean is supported by his published work and multiple independent institutional records; McClean occurs in the input and an older Cambridge item. Exact birth and death days, months and birthplace remain unverified. The 1905 and 1991 source values are corroborated and retained. Auction provenance and historical Geneva residence do not settle principal residence at death.

Forbes was checked first. Parent and completion research covered LinkedIn, Instagram, personal websites, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok, Wikipedia, Vimeo, Flickr, Trip Advisor and Zillow. No attributable personal profile was verified. A company and an institute have Wikipedia entries, but neither is his personal profile. Institutional websites are not substituted for his own.

Medical qualification does not make him a practising physician or establish healthcare wealth. Consumer electronics and Art collector are the minimum supported active set. Auction accounts give different dates for the Leggatt exhibition; the dossier relies on the exhibited collection without asserting a date. No new taxonomy candidate is created.

Relevant BVWS and Billboard PDF bodies were read through public downloads in memory. Indexed publisher, Cambridge news and auction text supplied substantial source bodies where the direct reader failed or omitted fields; those access limits are recorded per source.
